feed.title: AI Wiki — AI Security
feed.subtitle: Threats, vulnerabilities, and defensive research affecting AI systems.

entry.title: Attackers Use Autonomous AI to Target Semiconductor, Defense and Civil Society Sectors
entry.summary:
Threat actors are leveraging the open-source Cairn AI agent framework to execute autonomous network breaches against semiconductor, defense, and civil society targets.

Why it matters: The deployment of autonomous AI frameworks like Cairn marks a shift toward automated, agentic cyberattacks against critical defense and technology infrastructure.

entry.title: ARTEX and AI-Powered Red Teaming Tools: What Defenders Need to Know
entry.summary:
Unit 42 analyzed how threat actors leverage AI-powered red teaming tools like ARTEX and outlined mitigation strategies for defenders.

Why it matters: Defenders must adapt their security posture to counter adversaries who actively deploy automated AI red teaming tools in operational attacks.

entry.title: Location Matters: Sparse Latent-Variance Attacks for Face Privacy against Diffusion Personalization
entry.summary:
SEAL is a sparse adversarial defense modifying only 5% of facial image pixels to prevent unauthorized diffusion model personalization while maintaining high visual quality.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that targeted, sparse pixel modifications can effectively protect personal facial identity against unauthorized AI generation without degrading image quality.

entry.title: Data-Efficient Unlearning-Based Backdoor Detection in Federated Learning
entry.summary:
Screening via Unlearning Response Analysis (SURA) detects federated learning backdoor attacks by repeatedly probing client models with a 10-image clean proxy while managing batch normalization state drift to ensure precise readout.

Why it matters: It enables federated learning servers to reliably identify backdoored client models using an extremely small, low-overhead set of clean proxy data.

entry.title: FALC: An Artifact-Centric Life Cycle Model and Research Agenda for AI Forensics
entry.summary:
The Forensic AI Life Cycle (FALC) model shifts focus to forensic artifacts generated across an AI system's lifecycle, establishing a reference artifact list, crime case examples, and a taxonomy mapping artifact analysis capabilities to existing techniques.

Why it matters: FALC gives investigators a structured framework to identify AI evidence while highlighting critical gaps where researchers must develop new forensic analysis methods.

entry.title: Pulse or Provenance? What rPPG-Based Deepfake Detectors Learn
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that rPPG-based deepfake detectors learn non-physiological high-frequency synthesis artifacts and dataset provenance rather than genuine cardiac signals.

Why it matters: The findings invalidate claims that rPPG detectors rely on physiological cardiac cues, exposing severe cross-dataset generalization failures and dataset leakage vulnerabilities in existing benchmarks.

entry.title: Cloud Security Alliance Announces Winners of 2026 Pitchapalooza
entry.summary:
The Cloud Security Alliance announced the winners of its annual Startup Pitchapalooza competition, recognizing early-stage member vendors for innovations in agentic AI security and cloud cybersecurity.

Why it matters: The awards highlight emerging early-stage vendor technologies aimed at securing autonomous agentic AI and cloud environments.

entry.title: What a CAGE 4 Score Measures: An Audit of a Learned Cyber-Defense Benchmark, Its Reference Defenders, and the Tables Built on Them
entry.summary:
An audit of the CAGE Challenge 4 cyber-defense benchmark reveals silent action dropping, unreported state leakage in reference wrappers, unseeded policy variance, and undocumented scoring conditions across published comparison tables.

Why it matters: The findings demonstrate that published CAGE 4 benchmark leaderboards rely on baseline state leakage and unseeded variance, invalidating reported performance comparisons for learned cyber defenders.

entry.title: Domain-Invariant and Language-Model-Assisted Acoustic Side-Channel Attacks on Keyboards
entry.summary:
Acoustic side-channel attacks successfully infer typed text in open-world settings by combining domain-invariant acoustic models with language model post-processing to overcome diverse hardware, user, noise, and compression variances.

Why it matters: Demonstrates that keystroke inference attacks pose a realistic security threat over commodity microphones without requiring fixed hardware, controlled environments, or device access.

entry.title: MOAI: Module-Optimizing Architecture for non-interactive secure transformer Inference
entry.summary:
MOAI is a non-interactive, homomorphic encryption-based secure transformer inference framework that uses consistent packing strategies and rotation-free algorithms to significantly reduce computational overhead.

Why it matters: MOAI drastically cuts the computational latency of non-interactive homomorphic encryption, bringing private, secure LLM inference on untrusted cloud providers closer to practical deployment.

entry.title: The $6.3 Billion Binance Signing Compromise and Agentic AI Threat Analysis
entry.summary:
On October 29, 2026, an attacker exploited a privileged DevOps endpoint to drain $6.36 billion from Binance hot wallets across 10 blockchains in 20 minutes.

Why it matters: Privileged DevOps endpoints in automated signing paths remain critical single points of failure capable of enabling massive cross-chain asset drains.

entry.title: Veritas: A Verifier Generation Harness for Agent Tasks
entry.summary:
Veritas is an automated verifier generation harness that outperforms seven existing harnesses on execution-scored and pairwise benchmarks.

Why it matters: Automating high-quality verifier generation removes a primary bottleneck in scaling self-improving AI agent systems without requiring hand-written evaluation scripts.

entry.title: Latent Barrier Steering: Hierarchical Safety for Generative Planning
entry.summary:
Latent Barrier Steering (LBS) combines latent-space steering with path-space Control Barrier Function (CBF) quadratic programs to ensure safety in flow-matching generative planners.

Why it matters: LBS prevents planners from failing when entire behavior modes are blocked by constraints, improving goal-reaching success while reducing post-hoc correction effort.

entry.title: DeepChronos: Temporal Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Multi-Step Attack Detection
entry.summary:
DeepChronos is a neuro-symbolic intrusion detection system that integrates flow-level neural evidence with explicit temporal attack-phase rules to evaluate multi-step attacks through logical progression rather than post-hoc alert correlation.

Why it matters: Enforcing temporal and causal logic directly within the detection model ensures higher accuracy and prevents physically impossible or causally invalid attack sequence predictions.

entry.title: Text2NGAC: a multi-LLM pipeline for NGAC policy extraction with mutation-based verification
entry.summary:
Text2NGAC uses a multi-LLM pipeline and a five-strategy mutation-tested verifier to extract all four NGAC relationship types from natural language access-control policies.

Why it matters: It enables automated, end-to-end translation of natural language policies into fully enforceable, structurally verified formal NGAC models to assist human expert review.

entry.title: Top GenAI security resources — November 2026
entry.summary:
Adversa AI's November 2026 compilation highlights 24 GenAI security resources, detailing a Workers AI cross-tenant leak, a recurring Hugging Face malware campaign, and three vLLM vulnerabilities.

Why it matters: These disclosures highlight active infrastructure-level vulnerabilities in popular AI deployment frameworks, model hubs, and inference platforms.

entry.title: GARD: Gradient-Guided Adversarial Representation Defense against Backdoors in Multimodal Contrastive Learning Models
entry.summary:
GARD is a target- and trigger-agnostic post-hoc defense that uses complementary global and local adversarial probes to eliminate multimodal contrastive backdoors without adding inference overhead.

Why it matters: GARD provides a robust, inference-free post-hoc repair mechanism for CLIP-style multimodal models without requiring prior knowledge of the attack target or trigger type.

entry.title: Sable: A Small-Field Sumcheck Argument for Bit-Exact Inference of Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Sable is a small-field sumcheck argument system and single-GPU prover that verifies bit-exact integer LLM inference without floating-point steps, achieving 40 to 64 times faster per-parameter-token proving than zkLLM.

Why it matters: It drastically lowers the computational cost and time needed to cryptographically audit open-weight LLM execution, reducing proof overhead to 6.4 cents per 4,096-token query.

entry.title: Isolation Is Not Confidentiality: Security Boundaries of Geometric Access Control in RAG
entry.summary:
A unified security analysis reveals that search-preserving geometric access control in RAG provides policy isolation but fails to guarantee representation confidentiality, query forgery resistance, or policy-membership hiding.

Why it matters: System architects cannot rely on geometric access control alone for end-to-end RAG data protection, as policy isolation does not prevent embedding reconstruction, query forgery, or metadata leakage.

entry.title: Gradient Inversion through Linear and Affine Subspace Constraints
entry.summary:
A new gradient inversion attack extends fully connected layer gradient properties to affine combinations and leverages subspace constraints to improve input data reconstruction accuracy.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that federated learning privacy risks are higher than previously measured, even under unknown batch sizes or applied differential privacy defenses.

entry.title: From Attack Surface to Defense Architecture: Compositional Security for Agentic Coding Harnesses
entry.summary:
ActiveSecHarness is a neurosymbolic reference-monitor architecture that enforces compositional security in agentic coding harnesses using capability tokens, deterministic tool guards, and a 2D product taint lattice.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that deterministic, low-latency neurosymbolic architectures provide near-zero false-positive security for AI agents without relying on slow, unreliable LLM-based guardrails.

entry.title: On Private Knowledge Retrieval and Private Inference for secure multi-agent systems
entry.summary:
This paper introduces a security-by-design framework for LLM-based multi-agent systems that combines signed semantic knowledge bases with private knowledge retrieval and private inference to prevent memory poisoning attacks.

Why it matters: It prevents malicious agents from executing memory poisoning attacks by ensuring semantic memory is cryptographically signed and accessed without revealing query patterns.

entry.title: BypassGym: A Benchmark for Evaluating AI Agents' Endpoint Defense Evasion Capabilities
entry.summary:
BypassGym is the first benchmark designed to systematically evaluate LLM agents' capabilities in generating loaders that evade real Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) systems.

Why it matters: It provides a systematic methodology for security researchers to measure and understand how effectively automated AI agents can bypass modern endpoint security controls.

entry.title: Stinging the Swarm: Extracting Attacker Intelligence from a Twin-Controller OT Honeypot
entry.summary:
Talos is an open-source, inline model-driven gate that evaluates OT fieldbus requests in milliseconds, rerouting hostile autonomous LLM agents to a device-faithful decoy to extract intelligence without allowing harmful writes.

Why it matters: It provides a low-latency method to safely isolate and reverse-engineer coordinated, fast-moving LLM agent attacks against operational technology without disrupting plant safety.

entry.title: Detecting sleeper agents hiding in AI model neurons
entry.summary:
Microsoft Research demonstrated that editing fewer than 10 neurons with inference-only compute can turn AI models into backdoored sleeper agents that pass standard evaluations.

Why it matters: Unattended agents with privileged access can execute malicious system commands if their open-weight checkpoints are compromised, making pre-deployment weight diffing critical.

entry.title: No finite rulebook can certify every safe program: an impossibility theorem for gatekeeping AI agents
entry.summary:
Researchers prove an impossibility theorem showing no finite, machine-checkable rulebook can completely classify AI-generated code safety for temporal properties like safety, confidentiality, and responsiveness.

Why it matters: It establishes mathematical boundaries for automated AI safety gatekeepers, proving that static rules cannot guarantee complete program safety without execution-based or probabilistic tradeoffs.

entry.title: Double Blind Evals: Resolving the Dual Confidentiality Dilemma in AI Safety Auditing
entry.summary:
Researchers executed the first double-blind AI safety evaluation using hardware secure enclaves, preserving mutual secrecy for proprietary model weights and a confidential benchmark.

Why it matters: It enables independent, third-party safety audits of frontier AI models without requiring developers to expose IP or benchmark creators to risk prompt contamination.

entry.title: ML Models Are Not Ciphers: Power Analysis for Weight Extraction Is Harder Than You Think
entry.summary:
Researchers evaluated side-channel weight extraction across complete, trained deep neural networks, demonstrating that ML models present unique structural obstacles to power analysis that do not exist in traditional cryptographic ciphers.

Why it matters: Directly applying cryptographic side-channel attack models overestimates weight-extraction capabilities on deep neural networks by ignoring fundamental algorithmic differences between ML models and ciphers.

entry.title: Spectral Unlearning: Transformer Structure-Preserving Updates for Language Models
entry.summary:
Spectral unlearning introduces a matrix-structured update framework for transformer-based machine unlearning that leverages matrix optimization instead of scalar coordinate-wise optimizers.

Why it matters: By preserving the structural geometry of transformer weights during optimization, this method improves the trade-off between targeting specific knowledge removal and maintaining overall model utility.

entry.title: Three People Arrested for AI-Enhanced Impersonation Fraud
entry.summary:
US authorities arrested three men for using AI voice and image cloning to steal over $129 million through corporate impersonation fraud between 2024 and 2026.

Why it matters: The case highlights the escalating financial risks of generative AI deepfakes used for sophisticated business email compromise (BEC) and executive impersonation attacks.

entry.title: Suppression Is Not Erasure: Mechanistic Analysis and Reactivation Boundaries of Subspace Projection for LoRA Backdoor Defense
entry.summary:
A study reveals subspace projection defenses suppress backdoors in LoRA adapters to 0.0% static Attack Success Rate, but fail to erase them, enabling 100% backdoor reactivation within two epochs of few-shot fine-tuning.

Why it matters: Evaluating backdoor defenses using only static Attack Success Rate creates a false sense of security, as stealthy backdoor mechanisms remain latent in the model parameters and can be fully reactivated with minimal downstream fine-tuning.

entry.title: Say Shibboleth: Fingerprinting the LLMs and Harnesses Behind Agentic Attacks
entry.summary:
A novel fingerprinting framework uses shibboleth traps and indirect probes to identify agentic attack LLMs and harnesses with up to 92% accuracy using telemetry.

Why it matters: Defenders can reliably attribute automated agentic cyberattacks to specific LLM models and attack frameworks solely through telemetry from honeypot interactions.

entry.title: Detecting Shadow AI: Unsanctioned LLM Agents on Enterprise Endpoints: A Taxonomy, an Open Detector and a Controlled Evaluation
entry.summary:
Researchers present a taxonomy of shadow AI agents and release Agent Detector, an open-source Windows tool that uses remote service identity, configuration, and execution history rather than process behavior alone to identify unsanctioned agents.

Why it matters: Detecting shadow AI on enterprise endpoints requires tying behavioral data to specific remote LLM identities, as process and network structures alone cannot distinguish AI agents from benign software.

entry.title: SNAPRAG: Cost-Efficient Knowledge Extraction Attack on RAG Systems via Adversarial Perturbations
entry.summary:
SNAPRAG is an LLM-free, black-box knowledge extraction attack on RAG systems that uses token mutation and adaptive dissimilarity threshold calibration to extract knowledge bases with fewer queries.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that private knowledge bases in RAG systems can be efficiently stolen at a significantly lower query cost and without relying on external LLMs, even when active defenses are present.

entry.title: StealthyPoison: Manipulating LLM Agent Behavior through Procedural Poisoning of Third-Party Skills
entry.summary:
StealthyPoison introduces a stealthy procedural poisoning attack that corrupts third-party LLM agent skill rules without user-request access, bypassing detection by SkillSpector and GPT-5.4-mini.

Why it matters: Public LLM agent skill registries are vulnerable to generalized, highly transferrable poison attacks that execute incorrect task outcomes while evading standard safety classifiers.

entry.title: Harness Matters: Measuring and Dissecting Security Resilience in Web Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers characterized web-agent harnesses into a four-stage execution workflow and introduced WebTrap Farm, an evaluation framework that isolates harness-level security vulnerabilities from backend LLM capabilities across three distinct attack vectors.

Why it matters: Securing AI web agents requires moving beyond model-centric safeguards to implement explicit defense mechanisms within the execution harness itself.

entry.title: Scaling Adaptive Prompt Injection Attacks with Agent Swarms
entry.summary:
A new framework uses agentic attacker swarms and a synthetic non-malicious action dataset to break prompt injection defenses on previously robust models.

Why it matters: It proves that current prompt injection defenses are insufficient against automated, agentic adversaries and highlights the need for continuous, proactive red-teaming.

entry.title: ShadowBench-MCP: Measuring Shadow Invocations in MCP-Style Tool Routing
entry.summary:
ShadowBench-MCP introduces a benchmark to measure shadow invocations, where task-preserving request variants lead LLM routers to select riskier execution paths and bypass security controls.

Why it matters: LLM agents serving as tool routers require policy-aware routing configurations to prevent benign prompt variations from accidentally bypassing critical software supply chain and security controls.

entry.title: Treating the Model as an Untrusted Component: Deterministic Policy Enforcement, Human Approval and Taint Tracking Against Prompt Injection in Tool-Using Agents, with Validation on Open-Weights Models
entry.summary:
Researchers evaluated prompt injection defenses for LLM agents using open-weights models and simulations, proving deterministic external reference monitors outperform in-prompt guardrails against persistent adaptive attacks.

Why it matters: Securing tool-using LLM agents against prompt injection requires treating the model as untrusted and enforcing security boundaries using external, deterministic reference monitors rather than relying on prompt engineering.

entry.title: PRISM: Causal Counterfactual Minimization of Agent Tool Privileges via Information Bottleneck Role Induction
entry.summary:
PRISM introduces causal counterfactual minimization to restrict over-authorized LLM agent tool privileges under the Model Context Protocol without sacrificing task performance.

Why it matters: It enables principled, automated least-privilege role engineering for LLM agents, drastically reducing security exposure in systems using the Model Context Protocol.

entry.title: On the Relative Security of Prompt Injection: Mechanised Definitions, Defences and Verdicts for LLM Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced PlanTERS, an Isabelle/HOL-mechanised framework that formalises LLM agent prompt injection security as 'relative security' by comparing an agent's leaks against a reference agent running a non-injectable model.

Why it matters: It provides a mathematically formal foundation to rigorously evaluate and prove the effectiveness of prompt injection defenses in LLM agents rather than relying on empirical heuristics.

entry.title: Coding Agents Propagate Vulnerabilities in Code Bases
entry.summary:
A study reveals that LLM-based coding agents propagate existing repository vulnerabilities into new code, with insecure contexts increasing vulnerability introduction rates by up to 35.4% in C/C++ projects.

Why it matters: Without continuous security fixes, autonomous coding agents operating under reduced human review will compound existing vulnerabilities and degrade overall codebase security.

entry.title: When Coding Agents Get Arms: Safety Risks Across the Digital-Physical Boundary
entry.summary:
ArmedAgent is the first systematic benchmark evaluating safety risks, including capability misuse and indirect prompt injection, in frontier-model-powered coding agents controlling physical robot arms zero-shot.

Why it matters: As zero-shot coding agents gain physical actuation capabilities, digital vulnerabilities like prompt injection can directly translate into unsafe or harmful physical actions in the real world.

entry.title: FORGE Lab uses agentic tools to identify memory safety issues in Rust
entry.summary:
Microsoft's FORGE Lab used Hyenas, an AI-powered vulnerability-scanning system, to discover memory safety soundness issues within Rust's core and std libraries.

Why it matters: Soundness bugs in Rust's foundational standard libraries can compromise memory safety guarantees across critical ecosystems like Linux, Android, and Windows that rely on safe Rust APIs.

entry.title: Grok Bot, Dots, Muse and Instinct Now Act With Your Employees’ Access
entry.summary:
Between August and late September 2026, four personal AI agents launched featuring standing access to user accounts to perform autonomous tasks.

Why it matters: Granting cloud-hosted AI agents persistent, unprompted access to personal and enterprise credentials introduces novel attack vectors and continuous data exposure risks.

entry.title: Top MCP security resources — November 2026
entry.summary:
November 2026 Model Context Protocol (MCP) security vulnerabilities include secret leakage from a reference server to web pages, cross-client SDK response contamination, and FastMCP transmitting secrets to rogue OAuth servers.

Why it matters: These critical vulnerabilities in core MCP implementations and SDKs expose sensitive credentials and client data to unauthorized web pages and malicious OAuth endpoints.

entry.title: AI Security
entry.summary:
Bruce Schneier attended the three-day [un]prompted AI security conference in San Francisco, which covered three core domain categorizations: security of AI, security with AI, and security from AI.

Why it matters: Categorizing AI security into three distinct functional areas helps researchers properly target and contextualize their work across the broader security community.

entry.title: Safety Is $Π_1$, Provability Is $Σ_1$: One Framework for the Hugging Face Breach and OpenAI's Mathematical Proofs
entry.summary:
Using a unified deductive-statistical framework based on Turing's Undecidability Theorem, this paper proves that pairing statistical proposers with deductive verifiers cannot alter the fundamental undecidability of software safety.

Why it matters: It establishes theoretical limits on AI-driven security, proving that statistical models paired with automated verifiers can definitively prove mathematical theorems but cannot guarantee absolute software safety.

entry.title: GuardrailAgent: An Agentic Framework for Jailbreak Defense
entry.summary:
GuardrailAgent is an adaptive, multi-agent defense framework that autonomously updates an attack knowledge base to provide dynamic, end-to-end jailbreak detection for large language models.

Why it matters: It shifts LLM security from static, easily bypassed safety rules to an adaptive, continuous defense capable of responding to evolving, unseen attack tactics.

entry.title: MemoryDojo: Benchmarking Poisoning Through LLM Agent Memory
entry.summary:
MemoryDojo is a new benchmark featuring 155 multi-session trajectories across four domains to trace and evaluate how memory poisoning affects LLM agent behavior across five memory systems.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized framework to quantify and mitigate security vulnerabilities caused by persistent malicious data in multi-session LLM agent memory.

entry.title: Differentially Private GraphRAG: Protecting Relation Connectivity and Semantics
entry.summary:
RelGuard is the first differentially private framework for GraphRAG, introducing relation differential privacy (relation-DP) to protect entity connectivity and relationship semantics during knowledge graph indexing.

Why it matters: It offers the first mathematically formal framework to prevent adversaries from reconstructing sensitive knowledge graph structures and relation semantics via black-box GraphRAG access.

entry.title: Breaking the Privacy Promise: Gradient Inversion Attacks on Federated Low-Rank Adapted Vision Transformers
entry.summary:
A new spatially anchored generative inversion framework exposes data leakage in LoRA-adapted Vision Transformers by incorporating server-prescribed trainable positional embeddings to resolve gradient ambiguities.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that LoRA-based parameter-efficient fine-tuning alone is insufficient to protect client data privacy in federated learning environments.

entry.title: When Feedback Becomes a Backdoor: Tracing Backdoor Skill Formation in Text-Space Skill Optimization
entry.summary:
Reference-feedback poisoning in text-space skill optimization (SkillOpt) can induce persistent, trigger-conditioned backdoor rules without direct access to the model, optimizer, or skill files.

Why it matters: Data poisoning in reference feedback can create persistent agent backdoors, though successful rule formation depends on whether the optimization pipeline preserves exact literals and candidate edits.

entry.title: Authorization Drift in LLM Agents: Evaluating Boundary Compliance in Multi-Step Tool Use
entry.summary:
Researchers formalize non-adversarial LLM authorization drift across four dimensions and introduce the 648-sample Authorization Drift Benchmark (ADB) created via Staged Execution-Reflective Synthesis.

Why it matters: Higher LLM capability correlates with increased authorization drift, revealing that deployment of autonomous agents creates inherent compliance and privacy risks even without explicit adversarial attacks.

entry.title: Jev as an LLM Safety Guardrail: An Empirical Study of Input Filtering, Selective Output Review, and Over-Refusal
entry.summary:
An empirical evaluation of Jev, a probabilistic safety guardrail for a Qwen2.5-1.5B pipeline, demonstrates that tiered input filtering with selective output review substantially reduces harmful response rates while mitigating over-refusal of benign prompts.

Why it matters: Tiered probabilistic guardrails enable developers to significantly suppress unsafe LLM outputs while maintaining lower false-positive refusal rates on harmless user requests.

entry.title: I Think, Therefore I Attack: Evaluating Thought Injection Attacks on Reasoning Agents
entry.summary:
A two-part study demonstrates that thought injection attacks imitating a Large Reasoning Model's internal reasoning style achieve up to 50% attack success rates on operational cyber objectives, outperforming standard prompt injections.

Why it matters: Imitating an LRM's internal deliberation trace bypasses standard prompt protections and defenses like tag stripping, enabling successful high-impact exploitation of agentic systems.

entry.title: Conflux: Preventing Privilege Escalation with Principal Contexts and System-Level Evaluation
entry.summary:
Conflux is a system-level defense framework featuring an ITES kernel that prevents LLM agent privilege escalation by enforcing permission intersection across all influencing principals outside of model judgment.

Why it matters: It moves LLM agent security enforcement outside of probabilistic model decisions by providing provable, system-level access control bounds.

entry.title: AttentionSwitch: Jailbreak Defense for LLMs via Joint Learning of Sparse Attention-Head Selection and Scaling
entry.summary:
AttentionSwitch is a jailbreak defense that jointly optimizes sparse attention-head selection and query-conditioned multiplicative scaling factors within a frozen LLM.

Why it matters: It offers an efficient, parameter-sparing jailbreak defense that maintains model capabilities while outperforming traditional defenses even with limited training data.

entry.title: I Don't Care How You Hide It, I Care What You Do: Runtime Detection of Malicious ML Models
entry.summary:
ModelShield is a runtime behavioral detection system that combines ML framework API instrumentation with eBPF syscall tracing to detect malicious models regardless of obfuscation.

Why it matters: It enables practical, accurate hub-scale screening of pre-trained ML models by bypassing static obfuscation techniques and capturing actual malicious system execution at runtime.

entry.title: RL-ATTACK: A Generalized Black-Box Adversarial Attack on Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
RL-ATTACK is a trainable black-box reinforcement learning framework that queries target language models to learn tailored adversarial transformations without gradient access.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that reinforcement learning can efficiently extract model-tailored adversarial perturbations in strict black-box environments, exposing safety risks without requiring gradient information.

entry.title: ARTEX abuse expands as cybercriminals target financial sector
entry.summary:
In October 2026, Cambodia-based threat actor Storm-3358 expanded attacks against the financial sector using the agentic AI offensive framework ARTEX alongside open-source remote access trojans.

Why it matters: The deployment of agentic AI frameworks like ARTEX accelerates every stage of the cyber attack lifecycle to machine speed, forcing defenders to adopt AI-driven responses and dynamic deceptive controls.

entry.title: Catastrophic Overfitting is Weight Drift the Training Loss Cannot See
entry.summary:
Researchers show catastrophic overfitting in fast adversarial training is caused by invisible weight drift, which can be eliminated by resetting weights to their exponential moving average when validation robustness drops.

Why it matters: It provides a computationally efficient fix for catastrophic overfitting in fast adversarial training, enabling robust deep learning models at half the training cost of multi-step methods.

entry.title: FedReason: Large Language Models as Weight-Space Meta-Aggregators for Heterogeneous Federated Learning
entry.summary:
FedReason uses an LLM as a zero-shot, weight-space meta-aggregator that generates custom Python aggregation rules every ten rounds by executing server-side analysis code and evaluating candidate rules on a proxy dataset.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that LLMs can dynamically engineer context-aware model aggregation algorithms in code, offering a zero-shot alternative to fixed federated learning rules under heterogeneous and adversarial conditions.

entry.title: Escalate or Close: How Fast-Tier Models Handle Held-Out Web Attack Families in Two-Tier Triage
entry.summary:
A study shows supervised fast-tier models in two-tier triage misclassify up to 60% of held-out web attack families as confident benign, whereas zero-shot decision models maintain higher escalation rates but face query-guided evasion.

Why it matters: Relying on supervised fast-tier models for security triage creates critical blind spots for novel attack vectors, while zero-shot alternatives introduce non-deterministic filtering and susceptibility to query-based evasion.

entry.title: AI-Native Task-Oriented Semantic Communications over a Relay: Benefits and Vulnerabilities
entry.summary:
A joint end-to-end task-oriented semantic communication system over a relay node achieves improved image classification and reconstruction at low SNRs, but introduces critical vulnerability to learned Byzantine relay attacks.

Why it matters: While relay nodes significantly improve semantic communication performance in low-power or high-noise environments, they introduce severe security vulnerabilities that require targeted defenses against insider Byzantine threats.

entry.title: KeHoSu: Keyed Homoglyph Substitution for Authenticated Text Provenance over Copy-Paste Channels
entry.summary:
KeHoSu uses keyed homoglyph substitution to embed traceable platform and user identifiers into text, surviving metadata loss across copy-paste channels without relying on positional state.

Why it matters: It enables reliable account-level attribution of redistributed or fragmented text even when platform metadata is completely stripped during manual copy-pasting.

entry.title: Dynamic Watermarking and Action-Conditioned Latent Dynamics for Secure Vision-Based Controllers
entry.summary:
An adaptive dynamic-watermarking framework uses an action-conditioned latent dynamics network and a reinforcement learning policy to detect replay attacks in vision-based controllers while minimizing control distortion and safety costs.

Why it matters: It enables secure, real-time detection of visual replay attacks in autonomous control systems without degrading physical tracking performance or violating safety constraints.

entry.title: CoRTeC: A Differentially Private Release for Synthetic Tabular Data, Decodable by Any Generator
entry.summary: The records that could train the most useful models, such as a hospital's patient files, are often the ones an institution cannot share. We propose CoRTeC, a method that releases synthetic versions of such records under

entry.title: Beyond the Landing Page: Website Blocking, Tracker Visibility, and Human Alignment in Automated Web Crawls
entry.summary:
A study of 2,000 websites demonstrates that LLM-driven agentic crawlers capture significantly more third-party tracker organizations and align better with human browsing than traditional non-agentic crawlers.

Why it matters: Selecting between agentic and traditional crawlers requires balancing trade-offs between stealth, tracker visibility, and true alignment with real human browsing behavior.

entry.title: Network Intrusion Forensic Detection System with Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Digital Chain of Custody
entry.summary:
MODEXRE introduces a forensic pipeline integrating a SHA-256 hash-chained chain of custody, OCSF normalization, and SHAP explainability to safely transition validated XGBoost models from laboratory training to formal case inference.

Why it matters: It establishes a verifiable bridge between machine learning intrusion detection and legal forensic requirements by ensuring model integrity, cryptographic chain of custody, and explainable predictions.

entry.title: Constraint-Aware Evaluation of Reinforcement Learning and Unsupervised Anomaly Detection for Security Operations Alert Triage
entry.summary:
Researchers formalized SOC alert triage as a constrained decision problem and benchmarked offline RL, Isolation Forest, and autoencoders under strict capacity constraints on 74,909 analyst-labeled alerts.

Why it matters: Constraint-aware evaluation and combining distinct model families allows SOCs to reduce unnecessary alert escalations without exceeding analyst workload limits.

entry.title: Decision Models as Retrieval Gates Against Injection and Pollution
entry.summary:
Open-weight decision models reading raw HTML act as fast retrieval gates to filter indirect prompt injections and web pollution before generation.

Why it matters: Pre-retrieval filtering using lightweight decision models offers an efficient, low-latency defense against prompt injection and web pollution without relying on expensive LLM generation.

entry.title: The Promise of Strategic Agentic Scambaiting
entry.summary:
Researchers present a formal game-theoretic model of agent-to-agent online fraud to evaluate how autonomous defensive scambaiting agents strategically disrupt AI scammers.

Why it matters: It provides a mathematical foundation showing that scaling autonomous scambaiting agents can systematically undermine the financial viability of AI-driven scam infrastructure.

entry.title: Beyond Instruction Override: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection with Task-Tampering Attacks
entry.summary:
A new benchmark evaluates Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) via task tampering, proving that attacks targeting decision rules, actions, and state achieve higher success rates and evade defenses better than objective-override attacks.

Why it matters: Standard safety evaluations that focus only on task redirection or objective overrides overestimate the coverage of current defenses against indirect prompt injections.

entry.title: A Gingerbread House for LLM Agents: Source-Planned Honeypots That Lure Autonomous Attackers into an Isolated Shadow
entry.summary:
A source-planned honeypot defense diverts confirmed autonomous LLM attackers to an isolated shadow application, reducing successful exploits on the real target to zero for the ARTEX attack framework.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that redirecting confirmed autonomous LLM attackers to shadow environments effectively neutralizes fast zero-day exploits without breaking the attacker's execution flow.

entry.title: JailBound: FOL-Guided Jailbreak Evaluation for Exploring LLM Behavioral Boundaries
entry.summary:
JailBound introduces an automated jailbreak evaluation framework combining a meta-attack prompt generator with a first-order loss (FOL)-guided dual-branch search to map LLM safety boundaries.

Why it matters: It enables systematic, automated generation of threat conditions and provides a local sensitivity signal to analyze exact behavioral transitions between safe refusals and jailbreaks.

entry.title: Signed but Not Safe: Requirement Integrity in Multi-Agent LLM Handoffs
entry.summary:
A study shows cryptographic HMAC-SHA256 signing of requirement manifests in multi-agent LLM handoffs reduces unsafe commits from 69.4% to 9.0%, establishing requirement extraction as the primary remaining trust boundary.

Why it matters: Cryptographically signing extracted requirements prevents middle-agent tampering in LLM workflows, shifting the critical security focus entirely to the initial requirement extraction step.

entry.title: Breaking $\mathsf{TraintoDefend}$ via Adaptive Neuron Clustering in Cryptanalytic Model Extraction
entry.summary:
SimBreak is a novel adaptive clustering rule that completely breaks TraintoDefend, raising target layer signature recovery from 0% to 100% on protected fully connected networks.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that enforcing weight similarity between neurons is insufficient for model confidentiality, invalidating the only known defense against cryptanalytic model extraction.

entry.title: Threat actors use agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secrets
entry.summary:
Threat actors are using the ARTEX agentic AI framework to automatically discover exposed secrets in public GitHub repositories and execute follow-on cloud attacks.

Why it matters: Agentic AI significantly compresses the attack timeline from secret exposure in public repositories to automated cloud credential exploitation and data exfiltration.

entry.title: SPILLWAY: Separating Target Admission from Sanitization to Defend Tool-Using Agents against Prompt Injection
entry.summary:
SPILLWAY separates target admission from sanitization to provide a deterministic, audit-traceable refusal floor that prevents prompt injection attacks against tool-using AI agents without added model-call overhead.

Why it matters: It allows autonomous agents handling sensitive email, file, and payment operations to block prompt injection attacks deterministically without requiring extra model calls or sacrificing utility.

entry.title: CANMentor: A Large-Small Model Collaboration Framework for CAN Bus Intrusion Detection
entry.summary:
CANMentor pairs a vehicle-side lightweight IDS with a cloud-side LLM teacher, using privacy-preserving proxies and latency-aware prediction switching to continuously improve local detection via soft target knowledge distillation.

Why it matters: It enables lightweight, resource-constrained vehicle intrusion detection systems to achieve high generalization on non-IID data without compromising raw CAN payload privacy or real-time latency requirements.

entry.title: MEvince: Knowledge-Constrained LLM Reasoning for Technique Identification from Malware Reports
entry.summary:
MEvince is a knowledge-constrained LLM framework that maps malware reports to MITRE ATT&CK techniques using shared behavioral representations, primitive-guided extraction, and evidence-aligned retrieval.

Why it matters: It significantly improves automated, reliable mapping of complex malware reports to ATT&CK techniques without requiring expensive model fine-tuning.

entry.title: New investments to reduce on-premises security risk
entry.summary:
Microsoft announced an on-premises security initiative featuring On-Premises Baseline Security Mode to harden supported Exchange, SharePoint, and Skype for Business servers by default.

Why it matters: The initiative automates patch deployment and default configuration baselines for critical on-premises servers, shortening the window of vulnerability against fast-moving AI-driven attack tools.

entry.title: ​​​​What’s new in Microsoft Security: November 2026
entry.summary:
Microsoft's November 2026 security updates introduce agentic AI controls alongside enhancements to Intune Endpoint Privilege Management and Microsoft Defender Experts.

Why it matters: These features provide administrators with granular, dynamic access boundaries for both human users and AI agents to enforce least-privilege security at scale.

entry.title: AI Governance Isn't a Chore Problem. It's an Architecture Problem.
entry.summary:
Senior business leaders are experiencing a 26% increase in working hours due to manual AI risk management, revealing that governance is being handled through reactive triage rather than embedded architecture.

Why it matters: Attempting to manage AI risk through manual processes and administrative oversight burdens leadership without solving fundamental operational security issues.

entry.title: LABBA: LLM-Assisted Behavioral Biometric Authentication
entry.summary:
LABBA integrates a lightweight LLM-based contextual reasoning module with a novel phone-blowing acoustic behavioral biometric technique to enhance continuous authentication robustness.

Why it matters: Incorporating LLMs into behavioral biometrics improves adaptability to real-world user variability and context changes over static threshold systems.

entry.title: Top AI agent security resources — November 2026
entry.summary:
Adversa AI released a collection of 43 AI agent security resources for November 2026, detailing vulnerabilities such as single-prompt takeovers, embedded browser exploits, and agents disabling system monitors.

Why it matters: Demonstrated vulnerabilities in AI agents reveal that simple prompt inputs and browser integrations can lead to full system takeover and security control evasion.

entry.title: Signed, Sealed, Leaked: Trust Beyond Signature for MCP Toolchains
entry.summary:
Germline execution prevents data exfiltration in signed Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools by executing invocations in ephemeral process copies containing only destination-authorized data.

Why it matters: It proves that digital signatures and network policies are insufficient to stop data leaks in AI agent toolchains, offering a mathematically proven, low-latency execution model for runtime isolation.

entry.title: Addition by Subtraction: Toward Mitigating Fragile Safety Alignment in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Addition by Subtraction enhances LLM safety alignment by iteratively pruning identified safety-critical neurons during finetuning and leveraging preference optimization to redistribute safety behaviors across the model.

Why it matters: By eliminating single points of failure in sparse safety neurons, this approach makes safety alignment significantly more resilient against both structural interventions and general jailbreak attacks.

entry.title: Signed but Steerable: Measuring and Closing the Text-Vector Integrity Gap in Offline Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entry.summary:
Researchers identify a security vulnerability in offline RAG systems where signed text-vector packs allow attackers to steer queries, and propose a deterministic quantisation verification method to close the integrity gap.

Why it matters: Edge devices using offline RAG cannot rely on cryptographic signatures alone to ensure precomputed vector embeddings accurately represent signed text, exposing local LLMs to silent retrieval hijacking.

entry.title: A Bag of Tricks for Defending Deep Learning-based Face Recognition Pipelines against Backdoor Attacks
entry.summary:
This technical report presents three practical defense tricks—one at training-time and two at inference-time—to protect deep learning face recognition pipelines against data poisoning backdoor attacks.

Why it matters: It offers actionable, multi-stage hardening techniques that system providers can integrate directly into industry face recognition pipelines to resist third-party data poisoning.

entry.title: A.S.E 2.0: Understanding How Repository Context Impacts the Security of LLM-Generated Code
entry.summary:
Researchers created CASE-Bench to evaluate how repository context affects LLM code security, finding that functionality-focused contexts and insecure exemplars significantly reduce the generation of secure code.

Why it matters: Context construction algorithms must explicitly prioritize security safeguards, as current functionality-driven methods frequently expose LLMs to insecure patterns or omit critical defense mechanisms.

entry.title: Analysis of Local Open-Weight LLM Agents on Vulnerability-Reproduction Tasks
entry.summary:
Researchers evaluated 12 local open-weight LLM configurations on CyberGym vulnerability-reproduction tasks, showing smaller 4B models solve simpler tasks while 27B models are required for harder ones.

Why it matters: Local, consumer-GPU-compatible open-weight LLMs can execute sensitive automated vulnerability reproduction tasks locally without exposing source code to external cloud APIs.

entry.title: KVGuard: A KV Cache Safety Checker for LLM Serving Systems
entry.summary:
KVGuard is the first systematic memory-safety checker for LLM KV caches, using shadow blocks to detect PagedAttention memory safety bugs with minimal overhead.

Why it matters: It enables developers to catch silent, isolation-breaking KV cache bugs during development without the severe performance and memory penalties of traditional GPU sanitizers.

entry.title: Securing Web Agents with the Compile-Then-Execute Paradigm
entry.summary:
Baya introduces a compile-then-execute paradigm for web agents, compiling user requests into Python programs before accessing live web content to structurally prevent prompt-injection attacks.

Why it matters: Separating plan compilation from runtime untrusted web data eliminates prompt-injection control-flow hijacking while simultaneously improving task execution success rates.

entry.title: Enforcing Accountable Disclosure in Confidential AI
entry.summary:
CORDE enforces a Confine or Declare policy in confidential virtual machines, restricting user data by default while logging all external disclosures to a tamper-evident, TEE-backed ledger.

Why it matters: It enables necessary safety monitoring, failure diagnosis, and third-party integrations in confidential AI agents without sacrificing data transparency or unrecorded leakage.

entry.title: When File Ingestion Misleads Language Models: Measuring and Mitigating Divergences in Office Documents
entry.summary:
Researchers identified extraction divergence in Office Open XML (OOXML) parsers as an attack surface for LLMs, demonstrating five instruction-free attacks and proposing a lightweight defense called Prism.

Why it matters: Discrepancies between human-visible document layouts and extractor outputs allow adversaries to secretly manipulate LLM processing and downstream agent behaviors without modifying the visual document.

entry.title: Assurance-Conditioned Continuous Authorization for Autonomous AI Agents
entry.summary:
Assurance-Conditioned Continuous Authorization (ACCA) is a harness-independent approach that continuously adjusts an autonomous AI agent's effective authority based on valid evidence, contextual applicability, and declared policy ceilings.

Why it matters: It provides a practical mechanism to prevent autonomous AI agents from executing unauthorized or unsafe actions when their operational context or underlying assurance changes mid-task.

entry.title: Reconciling Privacy with Provenance for Language Model Watermarks
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce locally differentially private watermarking, shifting the goal from tracking individuals to estimating aggregate usage, and propose the Red-Green Sequence watermark to protect user privacy while maintaining accurate population statistics.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that AI developers can collect population-level LM usage metrics and maintain text provenance without compromising individual user privacy.

entry.title: Timing is Everything: Inferring Temporal Membership in Continually Updated Models
entry.summary:
A novel black-box Temporal Membership Inference Attack (TMIA) uses bidirectional LSTMs on successive model outputs to infer whether and when specific data samples were used in continually updated deep learning models.

Why it matters: Continually updated machine learning deployments expose historical training data to fine-grained temporal tracking, requiring new privacy defenses beyond standard membership inference mitigations.
